From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com

Liz — thanks for the questions and the sheet. I pulled together concise answers below and attached a small diagram to illustrate runtime caching vs. control-plane logs. Where helpful I've called out operational SLAs and the evidence artifacts we typically provide during vendor validation.

1) Geographic residence of data
- Inference inputs and generated outputs (in the hosted API) are stored transiently in the compute region that served the request. We currently operate production regions in us-east-1, us-west-2, and eu-west-1; customers may choose a preferred region via the control plane.
- Customer metadata (account records, billing, model configuration) is stored in the regional control plane mapped to the customer's tenancy and region preference.

2) Retention windows (hosted API)
- Request-level ephemeral cache / KV: default TTL is 60 minutes to support streaming retries and short-lived batching; cache entries are never persisted to long-term object stores.
- Short-term request traces (for debugging and telemetry): retained for 7 days by default; can be shortened on request via contract. Traces include timing, route, model variant, and anonymized token counts — not raw customer payloads unless configured.
- Audit / control-plane logs (account changes, API key lifecycle): retained for 365 days and backed up per our logging policy.
- Aggregated usage metrics and cost reporting: retained for 25 months for billing analytics.

3) Tenant erasure / deletion process
- Trigger path: erasure requests are submitted via the Console (admin erase), Support ticket with DSR tag, or as part of the offboarding flow.
- Execution: we run a coordinated workflow that (a) disables new writes and tokens, (b) removes customer-specific control-plane metadata, (c) purges associated keys/caches in the serving region, and (d) gaps any scheduled backups from that tenancy.
- Timeline: standard SLA is 10 business days end-to-end for hosted customers; expedited 3 business day option available on written request for enterprise contracts.
- Evidence: we provide a deletion report (CSV) showing objects/records removed and timestamps, plus an audit log excerpt and a certificate of deletion if requested.

Operational notes:
- Backups: automated backups are region-scoped and do not contain live ephemeral caches from serving GPUs; backup retention is configurable for Dedicated/Private customers but for hosted managed accounts default snapshot retention is 30 days.
- Replication: synced control-plane metadata sits in the customer's region and a secondary replica in an adjacent region for resilience (only relevant for high-availability tiers).
- Data minimization: we do not persist raw customer inputs in long-term stores by default. Customers can opt into logging of payloads for debug purposes; this is a per-account toggle with strict access controls.

Attachments: redwood-data-flow-diagram.pdf (runtime vs control-plane)

If you'd like, I can convert the above into the exact cells in your spreadsheet and upload a filled copy. Rough ETA for that would be this afternoon PST.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Liz — quick clarifications on a couple of implementation points Soojin raised:

- Traces vs. payloads: by default, the telemetry traces Soojin referenced include metadata and timing only; if AcmeCloud requires payload-level capture for a specific integration we will only enable that with signed instructions and a narrow retention window.
- Deletion evidence: the CSV we provide enumerates control-plane object ids (tenant id, api key ids) and timestamps. For hosted customers we cannot produce low-level GPU KV cache images (these are ephemeral and scrubbed); we instead produce process logs showing purge calls and resulting status codes.

We can add a one-page summary statement (signed) listing the artifacts we will deliver for your vendor pack: deletion CSV, audit log excerpt, and a console screenshot showing tenant status "Deleted".

Kimberly Park
Manager, Trust & Compliance — Redwood Inference
